classification.difficultyReason: Combines two angle-bisector ratios to prove a quadrilateral identity.

content.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral and suppose the bisectors of $\angle A$ and $\angle C$ intersect on $BD$ at $E$. Show that $AB\times CD=AD\times CB$.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral with both angle bisectors meeting diagonal BD at E; schematic geometry preserves all incidences.
spec.mathematics: E lies on BD; AE bisects angle BAD and CE bisects angle BCD.

answer.short:
$AB\times CD=AD\times CB$.

Apply the Angle Bisector Theorem in $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle CBD$.
answer.worked:
By the Angle Bisector Theorem in $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle CBD$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{AD}&=\frac{BE}{ED},\\\frac{CB}{CD}&=\frac{BE}{ED},\\\frac{AB}{AD}&=\frac{CB}{CD},\\AB\times CD&=AD\times CB.\end{align*}$$
